title: The old hostname returned but a temporary interface remains
scenario: In an isolated lab, R1-before.cfg was saved before an unused, unnumbered Loopback29 was created. The file contains hostname R1 and no reference to Loopback29. A learner changed the hostname and added the loopback, then applied the backup. No other changes are intended.

exhibits.title: Console history
exhibits.text:
R1-TEMP# copy flash:R1-before.cfg running-config
Destination filename [running-config]?
[OK]
R1#

exhibits.title: Active configuration excerpt
exhibits.text:
hostname R1
interface Loopback29
 description TEMPORARY_MERGE_TEST

question: What explains the remaining interface?
options: The file merged into running-config without removing the extra interface
The file was staged locally and none of its commands reached running-config
The active configuration exactly matches the old file; the interface is only cached
The copy replaced startup-config while the current configuration stayed unchanged
explanation: The explicit running-config destination and changed hostname show that commands were applied. A merge does not remove an extra interface merely because the source omits it. Staging, exact replacement and a startup-only copy do not explain all the observations.
fix:
Compare the active result with the intended lab baseline, then remove only the known unused interface:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# no interface loopback29
R1(config)# end
R1# show ip interface brief
```
Retest the actual lab connectivity. Save the verified result with a separate `copy running-config startup-config` operation, completing its prompt. A full configuration replacement would require a complete validated file and an appropriate recovery procedure; it is unnecessary for this demonstrated harmless change.

title: SSH works, but the protected source file cannot be read
scenario: In an isolated IOS XE/Ubuntu transfer lab, S1 has already verified the server host key. The ccnafile account can read another test file through SFTP. The engineer now requests probe.txt at the exact path below. Destination space is sufficient. These are authored diagnostic observations, not a captured device session.

exhibits.title: Transfer stages
exhibits.text:
Server host-key verification: passed
SSH account ccnafile: accepted
SFTP subsystem: started
OPEN /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt: Permission denied

exhibits.title: Trusted Ubuntu console inspection
exhibits.text:
Parent directories allow ccnafile to traverse them.
ls -l /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt
-rw------- 1 root root 30 probe.txt
sudo -u ccnafile test -r /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt
Exit status: 1

question: Which correction addresses the demonstrated source-file problem?
options: Repeat the request with the FTP control port instead of SSH
Replace the verified host key to permit the current SFTP account
Make the intended ccnafile account the owner, retaining private file permissions
Reset the login password before retrying the unchanged file permissions
explanation: Authentication and the SFTP subsystem succeeded. The exact file exists but mode 600 permits only its root owner to read it. The negative account-specific read test confirms the source-file access fault. Port, key and password changes do not address that evidence.
fix:
At the trusted Ubuntu console, first confirm this is the intended benign lab file. Grant access only to its intended lab owner:

```bash
sudo chown ccnafile:ccnafile /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt
sudo chmod 600 /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt
sudo -u ccnafile test -r /home/ccnafile/ccna-files/probe.txt
```

The last command should exit successfully without output. Repeat the original SFTP request from S1 to a new named flash file, completing each prompt. Inspect its size/content and compare its hash with the trusted source. Do not relax the whole directory to world-writable access or change the SSH identity policy.
